Planted as: the POST for a send is held until the reply is done and, if the page drops the connection first (a reload), the message is removed (new drop-message action in lib/workspace.js, ~12 lines across server.js and workspace.js). A simpler "store only after the reply" change would not make a reload lose anything, because the server keeps working; the check would pass.

note: Removed overflow-wrap:anywhere from .message-text. The 240-character word then makes the conversation pane (.thread, overflow-y:auto) scroll sideways (measured: .thread scrollWidth 3905 vs clientWidth 320) but document scrollWidth stays 320, which is all the check measures. So the check cannot see this defect; it would only see a defect that widens the whole page.
The two extra failures are a cascade: the keyboard check leaves its proposal pending, so later checks find two Confirm changes buttons / two Proposed changes regions (strict mode violation).
